title: Arithmetic theories: Robinson arithmetic, induction, and nonstandard models
summary: Compare Robinson arithmetic with Peano induction, and use compactness to obtain arithmetic models with elements outside the standard copy.
abstract: The usual rules for zero, successor, addition and multiplication correctly evaluate every calculation on natural-number numerals. Do those rules determine the natural numbers themselves? Robinson arithmetic gives seven basic axioms, but they even allow an extra element that is its own successor. Peano arithmetic adds induction for every first-order formula, including formulas with fixed parameters, and rules out that simple example. Yet compactness still produces a model with elements unequal to every numeral. Even the theory containing all true arithmetic sentences has such a model. We explain how this can coexist with induction: the standard natural numbers form an external subset of the model that no formula, even with parameters, defines.
